claims.statement: The Codex adapter is an advisory alpha pinned to observed Codex CLI 0.147.0 evidence on macOS arm64; it is not GA and does not make Codex a peer enforcement runtime.

No input currently available carries observed hook trust: a config-derived trust_level of 'trusted' yields TRUST_CONFIG_ONLY and keeps the mode advisory, so a live 'enforced' doctor result should be treated as a bug until Phase 6 supplies observed hook trust.

The packaging decision selects the hybrid boundary with direct as fallback: the plugin owns skills, hooks.json, plugin manifest and marketplace lifecycle, while the project adapter owns .codex/agents/*.toml, runtime state, and a bounded AGENTS.md integration.

check_codex_packaging requires the selected candidate to have an observed passing isolated-local-packaging-probe, rejects packaging evidence claiming runtime execution, and when runtime_execution is observed requires separate runtime evidence with three passing checks and a disclosed automation-vetted-bypass hook trust mode.
check_codex_packaging requires the matrix's packaging.plugins row to remain advisory with observed evidence and to point at the selected candidate's evidence file.

render_codex_adapter validates sources before rendering: the decision must be hybrid with observed runtime execution, the plugin manifest must equal the pinned contract, the checked-in Codex hooks.json must equal the hooks derived from settings.json, and the manifest skill/agent/hook inventories must exactly match the on-disk source directories.

Codex hook registrations are derived from settings.json by accepting only five known events, requiring PreToolUse, rewriting the Write|Edit matcher to apply_patch|Edit|Write, wrapping commands as bash "$PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/...", adding additionalContextLimit 2500 to SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit and timeout 1 to SessionEnd.

Rendering refuses an output path inside the source repository or a filesystem root, refuses source symlinks, and emits a plugin tree (manifest, shared hook bodies, generated hooks.json, manifest skills) plus a project tree (.codex/agents/*.toml via render_agent_definitions.render_codex and .codex/harness-instructions.md) and a render-manifest.json.

Codex agent profiles are rendered as TOML carrying model, model_reasoning_effort, sandbox_mode, mcp_servers = {} for MCP policy none, and [agents] enabled = false when nested delegation is disallowed.

install-codex-harness.sh either uses --source or shallow-clones CS_REPO_URL/CS_BRANCH into a temp dir, then delegates to deploy-codex-adapter.sh forwarding codex-bin, codex-home, yes, overwrite-conflicts, dry-run and remove options.

The deployer registers the local marketplace agent-harness-local and plugin agent-harness@agent-harness-local only through the codex plugin CLI and records owned paths in .codex/.agent-harness/deployment-manifest.json; it does not directly edit .codex/config.toml or trust entries.

Managed project files are overwritten only when absent, identical, unchanged since the recorded install hash, or when --overwrite-conflicts is set; otherwise the local file is kept and the candidate is written as <path>.harness-incoming and recorded as a sidecar, with the AGENTS.md sentinel block following the same rule.

The deployer stages the full render before changing target state, moves the previous marketplace aside, and restores and re-registers it if marketplace add, plugin add, project sync fails, or a signal interrupts the run.
The deployer refuses the filesystem root as target, symlinked managed parent directories, managed paths escaping through symlinks, and a deployment manifest whose marketplace directory is missing.
Removal unregisters the plugin and marketplace and deletes only unchanged generated files and an unchanged AGENTS.md block, preserving edited files in a reduced deployment manifest.

check_codex_capabilities requires unknown evidence to have status unknown, an unavailable source, an owned exit_condition and no evidence path; documented evidence to cite an official OpenAI docs host; and observed evidence to use a version-pinned fixture whose runtime, CLI version, platform, closed-vocabulary capture label, observed status and config hash match.
The capability checker rejects any source whose expires_at has passed and, with --require-evidence, rejects load-bearing claims backed only by documentation.
In the committed matrix, config.project_trust, platform.linux and platform.wsl are load-bearing rows with unknown evidence, and supported_platforms lists only macos-arm64.

capture_codex_capabilities.sh captures only non-model CLI, doctor, dependency, config-hash and SessionEnd timing facts by default, leaving hook and custom-agent behavior unknown unless --allow-live-model-probe is supplied.

The doctor derives mode as unsupported if any unsupported reason exists (native Windows, missing bash/git/jq/python3, missing install, invalid manifest, unselected package), else advisory if any reason exists, else enforced.
The doctor emits PLATFORM_UNVERIFIED for any platform other than macos-arm64, so Linux and WSL cannot return enforced.

The doctor emits FEATURE_DISABLED unless hooks, multi_agent, plugins and unified_exec are enabled, parsing the live 0.147.0 doctor shape from checks['config.load'].details['enabled feature flags'], and emits DOCTOR_* reasons when codex doctor is unavailable, not ok, malformed, or has a failing check.

Install checks compare installed project files, hook bodies, hooks.json, plugin manifest and skill trees against the source checkout and the manifest inventory, producing INSTALL_HASH_MISMATCH, HOOK_COVERAGE_MISMATCH, SKILL_DISCOVERY_MISMATCH, AGENT_DISCOVERY_MISMATCH or PACKAGE_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH.

Evidence reasons are computed over platform-matching load-bearing matrix rows: expired rows give EVIDENCE_STALE, non-supported or unknown rows give EVIDENCE_UNKNOWN, documented-only rows give EVIDENCE_DOCUMENTED_ONLY, and zero matched rows give EVIDENCE_UNKNOWN; the config.project_trust row is skipped only when hook trust is explicitly trusted.

The doctor's config trust reader reads only the [projects."<root>"] trust_level from the effective CODEX_HOME config.toml, refuses files with multi-line strings or arrays, treats comments as scope-ending, and returns None (trust unknown) for anything unparseable.

The doctor runs codex doctor --json with a 20 second timeout (or reads --doctor-report), exports --codex-home as CODEX_HOME for the whole run so writer and reader fingerprints match, persists the record unless --no-persist, optionally writes Runtime-mode/Runtime-evidence-id into a SUMMARY, and exits 2 on input errors.

Runtime-mode records are stored at .harness-state/codex-runtime.json with a four-key fingerprint (install_hash, config_hash, cli_version, trust_hash) and an evidence_id of 'codex-mode-' plus 16 hex chars of a SHA-256 over the canonical record identity, which validation recomputes to detect tampering.

install_hash covers only harness-owned state (deployment manifest, its listed project files, marketplace tree) and config_hash covers both the project .codex/config.toml and the user-level CODEX_HOME (default ~/.codex) config.toml.
Runtime-mode records are persisted atomically via a temporary file and os.replace, and load_record returns None for missing, malformed or tampered records.

When reading the cached record, context_line recomputes install and config hashes and downgrades to advisory with STATE_INVALIDATED on any fingerprint change, and downgrades enforced to advisory with EVIDENCE_STALE once evidence_expires_at has passed, without re-diagnosing CLI version or trust.
The session-knowledge SessionStart hook only displays the cached runtime_mode context line and never runs the doctor or decides enforcement.
Run-state events may carry runtime_mode and runtime_evidence_id only as an all-or-nothing pair with a valid mode and evidence-id format, and chain validation rejects a forged or half-specified pair.

CI runs tests/scripts/codex-alpha-contract.test.sh, which composes the evidence check, adapter/agent render tests, install lifecycle test, doctor and runtime-mode tests, and a check that Linux/WSL cannot inherit macOS enforcement.
The committed runtime evidence asserts the hybrid runtime execution was observed with hook_trust_mode automation-vetted-bypass and that the direct candidate remains unknown and non-passing.
